evidence: Talk the Walk: Navigating New York City through Grounded Dialogue

evidence_levels.claim: We release a new dataset of 3,000 scenarios encompassing multi-agent visual and language navigation challenges.

evidence: Open-Vocabulary DETR with Conditional Matching

evidence_levels.claim: We propose ViLD, a training method via Vision and Language knowledge Distillation for open-vocabulary object detection.
ViLD achieves significant performance improvements, obtaining 16.1 mask APr and surpassing the supervised counterpart by 3.8.
ViLD is expected to achieve 26.3 APr when trained with the stronger teacher model ALIGN.
ViLD is anticipated to surpass the previous state-of-the-art by 4.8 on novel AP and 11.4 on overall AP on COCO.

evidence: Towards Robust and Reproducible Active Learning using Neural Networks

evidence_levels.claim: We will release all code and experimental configurations publicly to facilitate reproducibility and further research in the community.

evidence: Symbolic Music Generation with Diffusion Models

evidence_levels.claim: We propose Self-conditioned Embedding Diffusion (SED), a continuous diffusion mechanism for scalable text generation.
We demonstrate that our text diffusion models generate samples comparable in quality to those produced by standard autoregressive language models.

evidence: Behavior Priors for Efficient Reinforcement Learning

evidence_levels.claim: We introduce Attentive Priors for Expressive and Transferable Skills (APES), a hierarchical KL-regularized method that automates the choice of information asymmetry through data-driven, domain-dependent learning.

evidence: Is Support Set Diversity Necessary for Meta-Learning?

evidence_levels.claim: We systematically study the effect of task diversity on meta-learning algorithms across various models and datasets.

evidence: Emergent Communication Pretraining for Few-Shot Machine Translation

evidence_levels.claim: We propose a novel way to establish a link between emergent languages and natural languages through corpus transfer for downstream natural language tasks.
We demonstrate non-trivial transfer benefits for language modeling and image captioning tasks by pretraining on an emergent language corpus.
We introduce a novel translation-based metric to predict the transferability of an emergent language.

evidence: Asymptotic study of stochastic adaptive algorithm in non-convex landscape

evidence_levels.claim: We prove that the iterates of mSGD converge asymptotically to a connected set of stationary points with probability one.
We establish almost-sure asymptotic convergence of the iterates of AdaGrad to a connected set of stationary points.

evidence: How benign is benign overfitting?

evidence_levels.claim: We prove the first theorem establishing a formal relationship between label noise and adversarial risk for any data distribution.
We provide both theoretical and empirical evidence that uniform label noise is more harmful than typical real-world label noise.

evidence: Stochastic Security: Adversarial Defense Using Long-Run Dynamics of Energy-Based Models

evidence_levels.claim: We introduce three novel methods of MCMC initialization for negative samples within the Maximum Likelihood learning framework for Energy-Based Models.
We expect our methods to yield state-of-the-art performance in various tasks including image generation and adversarial defense.

evidence: Changing the Image Memorability: From Basic Photo Editing to GANs

evidence_levels.claim: We propose a fast and controllable approach to modify the memorability of face images using the latent space of StyleGAN.
We will further analyze how different layers of the StyleGAN augmented latent space contribute to memorability.

evidence: Quantifying Aleatoric and Epistemic Uncertainty Using Density Estimation in Latent Space

evidence_levels.claim: Our method allows us to disentangle explicitly aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties.
We demonstrate strong performance of the method in uncertainty estimation tasks on a variety of real-world image datasets.

evidence: Large Scale Private Learning via Low-rank Reparametrization

evidence_levels.claim: We propose a meta-framework for differentially private fine-tuning of large-scale pre-trained language models that aims to achieve state-of-the-art privacy versus utility tradeoffs.
We expect that the utility of our differentially private models will approach that of non-private models, achieving accuracy near 87.8% on MNLI using RoBERTa-Large under a privacy budget of ε = 6.7.
We will investigate the relationship between model scale and private fine-tuning performance, expecting to find that larger models are better suited for private fine-tuning.

evidence: Fully Decentralized Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Networked Agents

evidence_levels.claim: We establish the first finite-time convergence result of the actor-critic algorithm for fully decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning problems with average reward.
We propose a mini-batch Markovian sampled fully decentralized actor-critic algorithm and analyze its finite-time convergence and sample complexity.

evidence: Accelerated Single-Call Methods for Constrained Min-Max Optimization

evidence_levels.claim: We develop the Accelerated Reflected Gradient (ARG) method, which achieves the optimal O(1/T) last-iterate convergence rate for inclusion problems satisfying negative comonotonicity.

We show that a variant of the Optimistic Gradient (OG) method achieves an O(1/√T) best-iterate convergence rate for inclusion problems whose operators satisfy the weak Minty variational inequality (MVI).
We prove that the Reflected Gradient (RG) method achieves an O(1/√T) last-iterate convergence rate for constrained convex-concave min-max optimization.

evidence: Probabilistic verification of fairness properties via concentration

evidence_levels.claim: We construct AVOIR, an automated inference-based optimization system designed to improve probabilistic bounds and generalize prior work across a wide range of fairness metrics.
We will develop a novel visualization mechanism to help users investigate the context of reported fairness violations and guide them toward meaningful, compliant fairness specifications.

We conduct case studies applying fairness metrics across three different datasets, demonstrating how the proposed visualization and improved optimization can detect fairness violations more efficiently.

evidence: An Automatic Finite-Sample Robustness Metric: When Can Dropping a Little Data Make a Big Difference?

evidence_levels.claim: We develop polynomial-time algorithms for efficiently certifying the stability of Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression models against small changes in training data.
We demonstrate that our algorithms can outperform existing greedy heuristics in certifying model stability on the Boston Housing dataset.

evidence: FLAMBE: Structural Complexity and Representation Learning of Low Rank MDPs

evidence_levels.claim: We develop a novel model-based algorithm, RAFFLE, which finds an ε-optimal policy and achieves ε-accurate system identification with improved sample complexity.

evidence: Sequential Causal Imitation Learning with Unobserved Confounders

evidence_levels.claim: We introduce a new approach called Elf Distillation for learning from experts with asymmetric information access.
We derive necessary criteria for recovering the optimal policy from an expert with privileged information.

evidence: Optimal Regularization Can Mitigate Double Descent

evidence_levels.claim: We characterize the limiting bias and variance of ridge and ridgeless linear regression under high-dimensional asymptotics.
We prove that sample-wise multiple descent occurs when the spectrum of the covariance matrix is highly ill-conditioned.
We demonstrate that the ridge estimator with optimally chosen regularization can yield a monotone generalization risk curve, eliminating multiple descent under certain assumptions.

evidence: Min-Max Multi-objective Bilevel Optimization with Applications in Robust Machine Learning

evidence_levels.claim: We propose MORBiT, a novel single-loop gradient descent-ascent algorithm for solving min-max multi-objective bilevel optimization problems.
We present a theoretical analysis showing that MORBiT converges to the first-order stationary point at a rate of O-tilde(n^{1/2} K^{-2/5}) for weakly convex problems.

evidence: The Emergence of Objectness: Learning Zero-Shot Segmentation from Videos

evidence_levels.claim: We propose a novel approach to unsupervised object discovery in videos that directly processes consecutive RGB frames and infers optical flow using a layered representation.
Our approach is expected to demonstrate superior performance over existing state-of-the-art methods on three standard video segmentation benchmarks.

evidence: Black-box Smoothing: A Provable Defense for Pretrained Classifiers

evidence_levels.claim: We introduce a novel approach called ZO-AE-DS that combines denoised smoothing with variance-reduced zeroth-order optimization for black-box defense against adversarial attacks.
We validate the effectiveness of our approach on both image classification and image reconstruction tasks, demonstrating improved accuracy and certified robustness.

evidence: Learning the Pareto Front with Hypernetworks

evidence_levels.claim: We propose Pareto Manifold Learning, an ensembling method in weight space that discovers a continuous Pareto Front in Multi-Task Learning.
We expect to demonstrate that Pareto Manifold Learning will outperform state-of-the-art algorithms.

evidence: Global Convergence of Multi-Agent Policy Gradient in Markov Potential Games

evidence_levels.claim: We show that Nash equilibria and first-order stationary policies are equivalent in the context of stochastic games.
We derive a local convergence rate around strict Nash equilibria in stochastic games.

evidence: Taming neural networks with TUSLA: Non-convex learning via adaptive stochastic gradient Langevin algorithms

evidence_levels.claim: We propose a new class of Langevin-based algorithms for the fine-tuning of deep learning models that address known shortcomings of popular adaptive optimizers.
We provide a nonasymptotic analysis and full theoretical guarantees for the convergence properties of the TheoPouLa algorithm.

evidence: Train and You'll Miss It: Interactive Model Iteration with Weak Supervision and Pre-Trained Embeddings

evidence_levels.claim: We propose a new weak supervision approach called reinforced labeling (RL) that augments labeling coverage by propagating labels to uncovered samples based on inter-sample similarities.
We expect RL to yield considerable performance gains compared to state-of-the-art data programming methods, with anticipated improvements of up to +21 points in accuracy and +61 points in F1 score.

evidence: Sample-Efficient Reinforcement Learning in the Presence of Exogenous Information

evidence_levels.claim: We propose to use multi-step inverse models to learn Agent-Controller Representations for Offline RL (ACRO) as a solution to exogenous noise in offline visual RL.

evidence: Learning How to Ask: Querying LMs with Mixtures of Soft Prompts

evidence_levels.claim: We propose Context Optimization (CoOp), a method that automates prompt learning for vision-language models using continuous context representations.
CoOp demonstrates significant performance improvements over hand-crafted prompts, achieving approximately 17% average improvement at 16 shots.

evidence: Barking up the right tree: an approach to search over molecule synthesis DAGs

evidence_levels.claim: We will develop an amortized approach to generate synthetic pathways as a Markov decision process conditioned on a target molecular embedding.

evidence: Linear Disentangled Representations and Unsupervised Action Estimation

evidence_levels.claim: We develop a theoretical framework for unsupervised representation disentanglement grounded in Group Theory.
We prove three sufficient conditions that enable disentangled representations in an unsupervised setting.

evidence: Characterizing the Gap Between Actor-Critic and Policy Gradient

evidence_levels.claim: We propose a novel Actor-Critic learning scheme that improves stability and convergence by using a block diagonal approximation technique.

evidence: HV-Net: Hypervolume Approximation Based on DeepSets

evidence_levels.claim: We propose a novel deep learning architecture called DeepHV to approximate the hypervolume function in multi-objective optimization.
Incorporating symmetries into the DeepHV architecture leads to significantly improved model accuracy.

evidence: Architecture Matters in Continual Learning

evidence_levels.claim: We provide new insights into how architecture choice impacts the stability-plasticity trade-off in continual learning.
We yield concrete best practices and actionable recommendations for architecture selection in continual learning.

evidence: Towards Deeper Graph Neural Networks

evidence_levels.claim: We propose Deep Graph Multi-Layer Perceptron (DGMLP), a powerful approach implementing our proposed guidelines for building deep GNNs effectively.
We conduct a systematic experimental evaluation on the fundamental limitations of current GNN architecture designs.

evidence: A Mean-field Analysis of Deep ResNet and Beyond: Towards Provable Optimization Via Overparameterization From Depth

evidence_levels.claim: We establish that sufficiently large ResNets enable first-order optimization methods to find global minimizers, providing global convergence guarantees.
We propose a mean-field analysis framework that translates ResNet training into a gradient-flow PDE to examine convergence properties.

evidence: Latent Video Transformer

evidence_levels.claim: We propose a scalable autoregressive latent video prediction model that combines a high-fidelity image generator with a causal transformer model to achieve high-resolution video generation.
We introduce top-k sampling and data augmentation as techniques to improve prediction quality in video generation.
Our approach is expected to achieve competitive performance against state-of-the-art approaches on standard video prediction benchmarks while using fewer parameters.
